subject: Renewal acceleration + expansion — proposal for credit split and prorate
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Amy Torres <amy.torres@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal acceleration + expansion — proposal for credit split and prorate

Hi Amy,

Thanks again for the time on Monday — great to hear how the new inference pipelines are performing in production. You mentioned wanting to lock the expanded capacity now (additional 120M tokens/month) but keep Novamed's anniversary date at Oct 1 to simplify procurement. I put together a short proposal that balances (1) a partial prepaid uplift to secure capacity and (2) a prorated billing approach so you only pay for the months remaining in the current term.

High-level proposal: 
- Move forward with an accelerated amendment that adds the 120M token uplift today.
- Split the uplift fee: 50% invoiced as an upfront credit to reserve capacity; 50% prorated across the remaining three months (Jul–Sep) and then rolled into the Oct annual commit.
- Offer a one-time 7.5% renewal credit applied to the upfront portion in recognition of committing early.

I'll attach a draft amendment and a quick usage export so your finance team can validate numbers. If this looks reasonable, we can route the amendment to Procurement and schedule a short signature window to lock pricing and capacity.

Next steps I suggest: 
1) Quick confirmation from you that the split (50/50) is acceptable.
2) I loop Ben (sales lead) and Lauren (billing ops) to finalize invoicing terms.
3) Send an official amendment for countersignature — target sign by Jul 21 to avoid projected price uplift in Aug.

Happy to adjust the split if you need a different cash/cost profile — call me if you want to talk through other permutations.

Best,

Logan Wright
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0134

Attachment: novamed-renewal-accel-draft.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: usage-summary-q2.csv (csv)

From: Amy Torres <amy.torres@novamed.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novamed.com
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal acceleration + expansion — proposal for credit split and prorate

Logan —

Appreciate the clear proposal. The split makes sense directionally, but Procurement asked whether the upfront portion could be 40% instead of 50% (cashflow constraints this quarter). Also they asked how the 7.5% credit is applied — to net uplift fees or to base renewal? Finally, can you confirm the effective date for the additional capacity (immediately upon countersignature?) — we want to avoid a gap while legal reviews.

If you can sketch the impact of a 40/60 split (upfront/prorate) and clarify the credit application, Procurement is comfortable running this internally. We'll need the amendment with clear invoicing milestones.

Thanks,

Amy Torres
Director of ML Platforms | Novamed
amy.torres@novamed.com

Looping finance/billing here — short notes from my side:

- 40/60 upfront/prorated is doable; from an invoicing perspective we typically treat the upfront as a prepaid credit (applied to future invoices) and the prorated portion as a short-term invoice covering the remainder of the term.
- The 7.5% credit should be applied to the upfront prepayment (so it reduces the prepaid credit amount). This keeps ongoing rate cards clean for the annual renewal.
- Effective date: we can provision the uplift on countersignature. If Novamed needs earlier sandbox access while legal reviews, we can provision a soft buffer (read-only or throttled) but production capacity will require countersignature for commercial and SLA reasons.

Attachments for your review: estimated-invoice-breakdown-JulSep.xlsx (I uploaded a quick calc). If Amy wants the 40% upfront, I'll update the draft amendment and the invoice schedule and send back within the day.

-Ben

Amy — thanks for the quick turn. We updated the draft to reflect the 40/60 split and applied the 7.5% credit against the upfront prepayment line; numbers attached.

Summary of changes:
- Upfront prepayment: 40% of uplift fee, net of 7.5% early-commit credit.
- Prorated invoice: 60% split evenly across Jul/Sep remaining months (we calculated three months).
- Provisioning: Redwood will stand up the reserved capacity within 24 hours of countersignature; sandbox preview is available upon request while legal reviews.
- Invoice milestones: upfront invoice due on countersignature; prorated invoice schedule sent with amendment (net 30).

I'm attaching the amended draft amendment (novamed-renewal-accel-draft.pdf) and the usage export. If Procurement is happy, please confirm and we'll route the DocuSign link for signature this week.

If Procurement requests a PO number on the invoice, please send it to billing@redwood.com and Lauren will ensure it's included.

Best,
